parole.significato: a red wine produced in this area
parole.testo: From Sardinian Campidànu, presumably referring to the fertile land and related to campo (“field”).
Borrowed from Sardinian carasau (“toasted”), past participle of verb carasare, from Latin charaxō, borrowed from Ancient Greek χᾰρᾰ́σσω (khărắssō, “to carve, to engrave”).
Borrowed from Sardinian cozudu, colludu. By surface analysis, coglia + -uto.

parole.significato: a Sardinian institution about the use of grazeland
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sardinian, from Medieval Latin cursoria (“portion of grazeland”), originally a neuter plural, derived from Latin currō (“to run”), due to it indicating a portion of land where sheep were free to roam.

parole.significato: a type of grappa from Sardinia
Typical pastry of Sardinia, made with almond paste.
parole.testo: Sardinian gueffus, itself a Pseudo-Hispanism, derived from huevos. Sometimes erroneously claimed to derive from guelfo.

parole.significato: nuraghe (a form of megalithic tower found in Sardinia)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sardinian nuraghe. The ultimate origin is uncertain; possibly related to the Sardinian place names Nurra, Nurri, and Nurru, and the word nurra (“pile of stones”). Another possible connection is Latin mūrus (“wall”).
Borrowed from Sardinian [Term?], from Catalan tanca (“fence”).
